einzeiler: Building the software brains and development platforms that power physical AI machines.
kurzfassung: Applied Intuition provides software brains and development tools for autonomous machines across industries like automotive, defense, and mining. Co-founders Kassir Younis and Peter Ludwig discuss the massive potential of physical AI, their horizontal business model, and their new agentic platform, Dana. The company focuses on scaling safety-critical applications while remaining a core technology provider without building hardware.
stichpunkte: Applied Intuition builds intelligence and development platforms for physical AI machines across automotive, defense, mining, and agriculture.
Physical AI differs from digital AI due to real-time constraints, safety criticality, and strict cost and compute envelopes.
The company started with developer tools before expanding into operating systems and vertical autonomy stacks.
Dana is the company's new agentic platform designed to lower the barrier to entry for developing physical AI.
A massive data engine and feedback loop continuously improve model performance through simulation and reinforcement learning.
The business model relies on traditional software licensing rather than complex or innovative accounting.
Customers include 18 of the top 20 automotive manufacturers as well as global operators in mining, defense, and robotics.

clips.hook: Why physical AI addresses dangerous jobs first
clips.text: Unlike digital AI where office workers worry about automation, physical AI rapidly targets physically demanding and hazardous labor in agriculture, trucking, and mining.

clips.hook: The massive economic valuation of autonomous driving
clips.text: Sophisticated market participants value Waymo at over one hundred billion dollars because the potential societal impact of autonomous technology is immense.

clips.hook: The mission to power a billion machines
clips.text: Dana represents the culmination of a decade of work, serving as an agentic platform that drastically simplifies the creation of physical AI systems.

clips.hook: Building a moat through high-quality data collection
clips.text: Gathering reliable data at scale requires a deeply complex technical stack, creating a fundamental long-term competitive advantage.
The company relies on straightforward software licensing for its revenue while driving radical innovation purely on the technology side.

beschreibung:
Today, we are breaking down Applied Intuition. Our guests are co-founders Qasar Younis and Peter Ludwig, who started the company in 2017 with a mission to make a billion machines intelligent.

The simplest way to understand Applied Intuition is that it builds the brains for machines, and the tools other companies use to build those brains.

If a manufacturer wants its tractor, truck, or mining vehicle to drive itself, it can buy the intelligence from Applied Intuition or use its platform to develop its own. The analogy the founders use is Nvidia.

Just as Nvidia sells chips into everyone else's machines, Applied Intuition sells intelligence into everyone else's machines, across automotive, defense, mining, agriculture, and robotics, without building any single machine itself.

We discuss why the most important companies of the next 25 years will all be physical AI companies, Dana, their new agentic platform for developing and deploying these systems, and how the company raised a billion dollars without spending any of it.

Please enjoy this Breakdown of Applied Intuition.
